Hi @jiyfhust. Thanks for your PR.

I'm waiting for a [pingcap](https://github.com/orgs/pingcap/people) member to verify that this patch is reasonable to test. If it is, they should reply with `/ok-to-test` on its own line. Until that is done, I will not automatically test new commits in this PR, but the usual testing commands by org members will still work. Regular contributors should [join the org](https://github.com/orgs/pingcap/people) to skip this step.

Once the patch is verified, the new status will be reflected by the `ok-to-test` label.

I understand the commands that are listed [here](https://go.k8s.io/bot-commands?repo=pingcap%2Ftidb).

</details>

issue_context.title: this seems can be replaced by "select 1" to avoid scan whole table in some case
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/29727caacb882e0fdb5c8b540d77505e88950b4a/ddl/constraint.go#L358

```
from:
select count(1) from `%s`.`%s` where not %s limit 1
to: 
select 1 from `%s`.`%s` where not %s limit 1
```

review_comments:
* Ummm, could you please tell me in which case can avoid scan whole table. 
* And in my opinion, `select 1` can surly avoid aggregation like this: 
```
mysql> explain select count(1) from test.t where not a > 0 limit 1;
+--------------------------------+----------+-----------+---------------+---------------------------------+
| id                             | estRows  | task      | access object | operator info                   |
+--------------------------------+----------+-----------+---------------+---------------------------------+
| Limit_11                       | 1.00     | root      |               | offset:0, count:1               |
| └─HashAgg_19                   | 1.00     | root      |               | funcs:count(Column#4)->Column#3 |
|   └─TableReader_20             | 1.00     | root      |               | data:HashAgg_12                 |
|     └─HashAgg_12               | 1.00     | cop[tikv] |               | funcs:count(1)->Column#4        |
|       └─Selection_18           | 3323.33  | cop[tikv] |               | le(test.t.a, 0)                 |
|         └─TableFullScan_17     | 10000.00 | cop[tikv] | table:t       | keep order:false, stats:pseudo  |
+--------------------------------+----------+-----------+---------------+---------------------------------+
6 rows in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> explain select 1 from test.t where not a > 0 limit 1;
+--------------------------------+---------+-----------+---------------+--------------------------------+
| id                             | estRows | task      | access object | operator info                  |
+--------------------------------+---------+-----------+---------------+--------------------------------+
| Projection_7                   | 1.00    | root      |               | 1->Column#3                    |
| └─Limit_8                      | 1.00    | root      |               | offset:0, count:1              |
|   └─TableReader_13             | 1.00    | root      |               | data:Limit_12                  |
|     └─Limit_12                 | 1.00    | cop[tikv] |               | offset:0, count:1              |
|       └─Selection_11           | 1.00    | cop[tikv] |               | le(test.t.a, 0)                |
|         └─TableFullScan_10     | 3.01    | cop[tikv] | table:t       | keep order:false, stats:pseudo |
+--------------------------------+---------+-----------+---------------+--------------------------------+
6 rows in set (0.01 sec)
```
this also helps

```
select count(1) from test.t where not a > 0 limit 1;
will count the whole table before the sql return.

while, select 1 from test.t where not a > 0 limit 1;
will return when meet one row satisfy the where contition.

```
so, it the sql can return fast when it find a row not satisfy check constraint.
Hi, have I explained this clearly? ^_^
